Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

up in the air phrase

undecided

also undecided, leave open, be undecided, still to be decided

classical

Cic. Cael. 48: tantum in mediō relinquam (Lewis & Short s.v. relinquō)
Tac. Germ. 46.6
Traupman p. 110: in mediō relictus

in mediō relinquere

relinquō, relinquere, relīquī, relictum, with in mediō

leave undecided, leave open

Latin leaves the matter “in the middle”, open to all, where English leaves it in the air.

Other words

  • pendeō, pendēre, pependī — be undecided, hang in the balance (of a person or a matter)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman p. 110: pendeō, to be up in the air

    Literally “hang”; of a person in doubt, often animī pendēre (see be in suspense).

Examples

  • quod ego ut incompertum in mediō relinquam

    which, as unverified, I shall leave openTac. Germ. 46.6

See also be in suspense, unclear.
